about.aboutContent:
Permits for Commercial and Non-Residential buildings.


Map Layers include below filtered data:


  • Nonresidential and Commercial Permits in Review
    • Permit Type: BB, BM
    • Subtype: Commercial, Nonresidential, Hotel, Office, Other, School
    • Permit Status: Open, Pending
  • Nonresidential and Commercial Permits Issued
    • Permit Type: BB, BM
    • Subtype: Commercial, Nonresidential, Hotel, Office, Other, School
    • Permit Status: Issued
  • Nonresidential and Commercial Permits Completed
    • Permit Type: BB, BM
    • Subtype: Commercial, Nonresidential, Hotel, Office, Other, School
    • Permit Status: Closed
  • Hotel Permits Issued
    • Permit Type: BB, BM
    • Subtype: Multifamily Residential
    • Permit Status: Issued
    • Hotel Motel Units Created: > 0
  • Hotel Permits Completed
    • Permit Type: BB, BM
    • Subtype: Multifamily Residential
    • Permit Status: Closed
    • Hotel Motel Units Created: > 0
  • All Tenant Improvements (Permit Issued or Project Completed)
    • Permit Type: BY, BZ
    • Permit Status: Issued, Closed   
Note: The data shown in this map is updated daily. The unfiltered data source can be found by visiting the Bellevue Permit Data page


If you would like to have the complete data set going back to 1998 please contact OpenData@bellevuewa.gov and request the complete Permit Data set.

A tutorial on using our portal can be found here.

 

Below information provides additional instructions on working with the maps in the portal. 

 

Working with Layers


You can manage a layer and data view in the map by selecting the Layer List icon in the upper right corner of the map > select the 3 dots to the left of each layer. From here you will be able to manage views on the layer as well as add or remove the data within the layer by select View in Attribute Table.  


 


Attribute Table: 


The Attribute table provides the data contained within the layer selected. You can sort and filter on the data in different ways. 


 


Data Filtering and Sorting:


You can sort any column by selecting the column header and choosing sort ascending or descending. 


 


Select the Options drop down to enable advanced filtering, show or hide columns and export the layer data set to a csv file.
